purpose: Compare opening accounts and map phases without changing the frozen dossier, boundary, candidates, memberships or model inputs.

context_ocr.limit: Complete reports read as OCR context. Visual comparison covers cited opening selections on 12 OR pages, not every word on all 16 context pages.

assertions.statement: Buckland reports firing on April 4; Ricker explicitly describes that earlier affair as the opening fight of Pittsburg.

citations.quote: SIR: I make the following report of the affair of yesterday:
About 2.30 p. m.
quite a brisk firing commenced on the left of our pickets.
the opening fight of the great battle of Pittsburg.

assertions.limit: Buckland report dated April 5; Ricker heading April 4 [?] remains uncertain. Engagement segmentation must be explicit; do not move the frozen April 6 boundary automatically.

assertions.statement: Reed also narrates cavalry skirmishing on April 3 and a Saturday picket-post engagement near Howell.

citations.quote: During the Confederate advance from Monterey on the 3d there had been skirmishing between the cavalry of the two armies
another engagement with a picket post near Howell's on Saturday

assertions.limit: Later compilation. No underlying April 3/5 report or geographic identity has been adjudicated in this packet; these remain leads.

assertions.statement: Prentiss and Moore disagree on the Saturday reconnaissance composition.

citations.quote: five companies of the Twenty-fifth Missouri and five companies of the Twenty-first Missouri Infantry
three companies from the Twenty-first Missouri Regiment

assertions.limit: Do not merge company counts or assume a common patrol scope; no new troop quantity is created.

assertions.statement: Prentiss places Moore and five companies forward at 3 a.m., pickets driven in at break of day, and Moore wounded before 6.

citations.quote: At 3 o'clock on the morning of Sunday, April 6, Col. David Moore
at break of day the advance pickets were driven in
Shortly before 6 o'clock, Col. David Moore having been severely wounded

assertions.limit: November report after captivity; conflicts with April regimental reports are retained.

assertions.statement: Quinn puts an order for several companies at 3 a.m., followed by marching and contact; wounded arrived about daylight.

citations.quote: At 3 o'clock a. m. of that day several companies were ordered out
About daylight the dead and wounded began to be brought in.

assertions.limit: An order time is not an exact contact time. The opening passage does not identify Powell by name.

assertions.statement: Van Horn calls 3 a.m. the attack time and names Powell and three companies ahead of Moore.

citations.quote: the attack being made on its front at 3 o'clock in the morning
under Major Powell, were dispatched to engage the enemy's advance

assertions.limit: Preserve the literal attack wording rather than rewriting 3 a.m. as a departure time.

assertions.statement: Moore reports notification about 6 a.m. and an advance ordered by Peabody after pickets were driven in.

citations.quote: On Sunday morning, the 6th instant, at about 6 o'clock, being notified
by order of Col. Everett Peabody

assertions.limit: Does not synchronize with Prentiss or decide who issued the initial patrol order.

assertions.statement: Woodyard places the order to Moore before sunrise, identifies Twelfth Michigan pickets, and describes a cotton-field position after the junction.

citations.quote: before sunrise, General Prentiss ordered Colonel Moore
to sustain the pickets of the Twelfth Michigan Infantry.
the northwest corner of a cotton field.

assertions.limit: The unnamed field and reported directions are not georeferenced. This later junction is not automatically the first-contact location.

assertions.statement: Allen reports an encounter about 5:30 a.m. roughly one and a half miles ahead/right of camp and calls it the first enemy fire.

citations.quote: At about 5.30 a. m. on the 6th
about 1½ miles in front and to the right of our camp
This was the first fire of the enemy.

assertions.limit: Report date unstated. Preserve this competing first-fire claim; source-specific scope may differ. Do not equate it to an independently verified first shot.

assertions.statement: Hardcastle describes a battalion picket post ahead of the brigade plus advanced parties; cavalry shots occur about dawn before infantry fire.

citations.quote: a quarter of a mile in front of our brigade
200 yards in front of my center.
100 yards in front of my center
About dawn the cavalry vedettes fired three shots, wheeled, and galloped back.
He fired upon them and joined his battalion with his men.

assertions.limit: Report date is blank apart from 1862. It does not locate the vedettes or establish whether their shots were alarm signals, aimed hostile fire, or the first shots anywhere.

assertions.statement: Reed connects Powell with the southeast corner of Fraley field at 4:55 a.m. and gives later withdrawal to Seay Field; this is retrospective geographic/timing reconstruction.

citations.quote: near the southeast corner of Fraley field
Powell fell back before the advance of Wood's brigade to the Seay Field
at the corner of Fraley's and Wood's fields

assertions.limit: The two locational descriptions have not been surveyed against a common map. No contemporary clock calibration or independent derivation of 4:55 is established.

assertions.statement: Reed places Wood in Hardee’s center on Saturday night with Third Mississippi on picket and Harper’s battery behind the infantry.

citations.quote: It occupied the center of Hardee's line of battle Saturday night
the Third Mississippi on picket, and Harper's (Mississippi) battery in rear of the infantry.

assertions.limit: Relative location only; no exact polygon or complete personnel membership.

assertions.statement: Beauregard reports reconnaissance contact at 5 a.m. and movement at 5:30, with Hardee, Bragg, Polk and Breckinridge echelon descriptions.

citations.quote: At 5 a. m. on the 6th instant, a reconnoiteriug party of the enemy having become engaged with our advance pickets
At 5.30 a. m. our lines and columns were in motion
The second line, composed of the other troops of Bragg's corps, followed the first at a distance of 500 yards

assertions.limit: Previously pinned text re-inspected, no new p386 facsimile audit. Army-level report cannot resolve earlier picket shots or prove all formations were in those positions immediately before contact.

assertions.statement: Beauregard describes cavalry and four artillery pieces already forward at three fords, while Maney’s reinforcement is associated with the movement order.

citations.quote: regiment of cavalry atrd battery of four pieces already thrown forward to watch and guard Greer's, Tan ner's, and Borland's Fords, on Lick Creek

assertions.limit: Guard identities, exact B0 census and Borland map identity remain unresolved. Do not treat Maney’s ordered movement as completed pre-contact presence.

map_readings.statement: Blue morning and red night lines distinguish six local Union command labels (Sherman, Prentiss, McClernand, Hurlbut, W. H. L. Wallace and Stuart); red Lew Wallace/Buell and river gunboats must not be moved into the opening state. North is right.
map_readings.limit: Morning is not a pre-contact instant. Catalog dates the map [1862] via Stephenson 1989; drawing/compilation time and underlying survey unestablished.
map_readings.coordinate_system: pixels in original full-resolution JPEG, top-left origin; inspection windows only, not geographic coordinates

map_readings.statement: The April 6–7 map depicts Hardee, Bragg, Polk and Breckinridge lines, Union camps and gunboats; Tanner and Greer ford labels are legible.
map_readings.limit: No phase-specific clock in the inspected legend; not a B0 census. Beauregard endorsement ties it to the same reporting chain. Borland identification and full guard distribution remain open.
map_readings.coordinate_system: pixels in original full-resolution JPEG, top-left origin; inspection windows only, not geographic coordinates

open_gates.question: Does the engagement boundary include April 3–5 contacts?
open_gates.next_evidence: Inspect the April 4 Hardee/Jordan/Sherman reports and the referenced April 5 Howell encounter; compare event continuity before amending any boundary.

open_gates.question: Which April 6 shot/contact qualifies first under the chosen rule?
open_gates.next_evidence: Trace Reed’s 4:55 derivation and patrol testimony, identify cavalry vedettes, and distinguish alarm shots, departure times and separate patrols.

open_gates.question: What is the exact geographic area and complete location inventory?
open_gates.next_evidence: Tie field-name variants, camp plots, guard detachments, approach columns and reserves to a common survey with reported-time uncertainty; identify Borland ford.

open_gates.question: How are afloat personnel classified consistently on both sides?
open_gates.next_evidence: Recover April 5–6 transport/gunboat deck logs and landing times; choose a bank/water boundary and apply a symmetrical physical-availability rule. Map boat icons cannot establish opening crew membership.

open_gates.question: Can the seven blocked observations be mapped to complete B0 populations?
open_gates.next_evidence: After G1–G4, audit roster/return inclusions, absences, detached guards and overlapping totals. No new arithmetic repairs.
